title: Factors That Contribute to the Widespread of Fake News & Misinformation

cues.en: Hello guys.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: Welcome back to the course.
cues.zh: 歡迎回到課程。

cues.en: In this video we are going to talk about six different factors that contribute to the widespread of fake news and misinformation.
cues.zh: 這支影片將介紹促使假新聞及錯誤資訊廣泛流傳的六個因素。

cues.en: So you might be wondering why would people want to spread fake news and misinformation.
cues.zh: 你可能會想，為什麼有人想散布假新聞與錯誤資訊？

cues.en: What is the reasoning behind that?
cues.zh: 背後的原因是什麼？

cues.en: Okay, so now let's talk about the first one here.
cues.zh: 先看第一項。

cues.en: Clickbait incentives.
cues.zh: 誘導點擊的獎勵機制。

cues.en: So news outlets and websites may create sensational or misleading headlines to attract more clicks and generate advertising revenue, often at the expense of accuracy.
cues.zh: 新聞媒體或網站可能製作聳動或誤導性的標題，吸引更多點擊、賺取廣告收入，往往犧牲了準確性。

cues.en: So think about this, guys.
cues.zh: 想像一下。

cues.en: If the title of the news is very boring, then obviously not a lot of people will click on that link.
cues.zh: 如果新聞標題非常無聊，顯然不會有很多人點進去。

cues.en: That's the reason why a news outlet will need to make the title to be very interesting and sometimes controversial, because the objective here is to get as many clicks as possible, right?
cues.zh: 因此，新聞媒體必須讓標題吸引人，有時甚至帶有爭議，因為目標是盡可能取得更多點擊。

cues.en: But in some cases, the news outlet make the title that doesn't really align with the reality, make the news title that doesn't really reflect the reality.
cues.zh: 但有時候，媒體製作的標題不符合實際情況，無法反映事實。

cues.en: So that's going to mislead people.
cues.zh: 這就會誤導閱聽人。

cues.en: But apparently some news outlet didn't really care because their objective here is very clear.
cues.zh: 有些媒體似乎不在乎，因為它們的目標很清楚。

cues.en: They want to get a lot of clicks.
cues.zh: 就是取得大量點擊。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So now let's move on to the second one here.
cues.zh: 接著看第二項。

cues.en: Confirmation bias.
cues.zh: 確認偏誤。

cues.en: So people may be inclined to believe and share information that aligns with their existing beliefs, leading to the spread of biased or false content.
cues.zh: 人們可能傾向相信並分享符合既有信念的資訊，導致帶有偏差或虛假的內容傳播。

cues.en: So some people out there, they are not willing to challenge their belief.
cues.zh: 有些人不願意挑戰自己的信念。

cues.en: They only want to consume content that aligns with their value, that aligns with their beliefs.
cues.zh: 只想接觸符合自己價值觀與信念的內容。

cues.en: So they only want to listen to podcasts that they want to hear.
cues.zh: 只想聽自己想聽的 Podcast。

cues.en: They only want to watch videos that they want to see.
cues.zh: 只想看自己想看的影片。

cues.en: So that's what created confirmation bias, guys.
cues.zh: 這就形成了確認偏誤。

cues.en: And a lot of people do not realize that okay.
cues.zh: 而且很多人沒有察覺。

cues.en: So now let's talk about the third one here.
cues.zh: 接著看第三項。

cues.en: Political manipulation.
cues.zh: 政治操弄。

cues.en: So political actors may spread false information to discredit opponents or advance their own agendas contributing to misinformation in the public sphere.
cues.zh: 政治行為者可能散布虛假資訊，抹黑對手或推動自己的議程，使公共領域出現錯誤資訊。

cues.en: So almost like every single elections there will always be a fake news, right?
cues.zh: 幾乎每次選舉，都會有假新聞出現。

cues.en: So a lot of political activists using social media to spread fake news.
cues.zh: 很多政治活動人士會利用社群媒體散布假新聞。

cues.en: That's the reason why, when it comes to political news, you guys need to do your own research.
cues.zh: 因此，看到政治新聞時，應該自行研究。

cues.en: You guys need to do your own due diligence.
cues.zh: 做好查證。

cues.en: You guys need to check if that news is real or fake, because sometimes it's kind of hard and challenging to distinguish like which one is real?
cues.zh: 檢查新聞是真是假，因為有時候很難分辨，哪個是真的？

cues.en: Which one is fake?
cues.zh: 哪個是假的？

cues.en: Okay, so now let's move on to the next one here.
cues.zh: 接著看下一項。

cues.en: Social media echo chamber.
cues.zh: 社群媒體同溫層。

cues.en: So social media algorithm can create echo chambers where individuals are exposed to information that reinforces their existing view, potentially amplifying fake news okay.
cues.zh: 社群媒體演算法可能形成同溫層，讓人接觸到強化既有觀點的資訊，進而放大假新聞。

cues.en: So let me explain guys.
cues.zh: 我來解釋。

cues.en: So for example you are on TikTok and you watch a lot of videos about certain political content.
cues.zh: 例如，你在 TikTok 觀看很多某類政治內容的影片。

cues.en: The more videos that you watch, TikTok algorithm is going to be trained to recommend you more videos similar to that particular content.
cues.zh: 看得越多，TikTok 演算法就越會推薦類似內容。

cues.en: So the more content that you consume, it's going to be harder for you to detect if there is any fake
cues.zh: 接觸的內容越多，就可能越難辨識其中的假

cues.en: news, because you are subconsciously conditioned to believe that anything that you watch is true.
cues.zh: 新聞，因為你已在潛意識中被制約，相信看到的一切都是真的。

cues.en: Anything that you watch is real, right?
cues.zh: 相信自己看到的都是真實的。

cues.en: So that's the reason why social media echo chambers is actually not a good thing.
cues.zh: 因此，社群媒體同溫層其實不是好事。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So now let's move on to the next one here.
cues.zh: 接著看下一項。

cues.en: Sensationalism.
cues.zh: 聳動化。

cues.en: Sensationalizing news stories by exaggerating details or presenting them in an attention grabbing manner
cues.zh: 誇大細節，或以吸引注意的方式呈現新聞，

cues.en: can lead to the spread of inaccurate or misleading information.
cues.zh: 可能造成不準確或誤導性資訊傳播。

cues.en: So actually, sensationalism is very similar to clickbait incentives, right?
cues.zh: 其實，聳動化和誘導點擊的獎勵機制很相似。

cues.en: Because you want to get a lot of clicks, right?
cues.zh: 因為你希望獲得很多點擊。

cues.en: You want to get a lot of people watching your videos.
cues.zh: 希望很多人觀看你的影片。

cues.en: So you create a very controversial title that might not be accurate, that might not reflect or align with what's really happening.
cues.zh: 因此製作極具爭議、卻可能不準確，或無法反映實際情況的標題。

cues.en: So yeah, it can potentially lead to fake news too.
cues.zh: 這也可能造成假新聞。

cues.en: And finally, the last one here profit motives.
cues.zh: 最後一項是獲利動機。

cues.en: Some individuals or organizations create fake news to serve their financial interests, such as selling products or manipulating stock prices.
cues.zh: 有些個人或組織製作假新聞，是為了自己的經濟利益，例如銷售產品或操縱股價。

cues.en: So let me give you an example here.
cues.zh: 我舉個例子。

cues.en: So let's say you own a company and you sell a product and you create an article and post it on your website.
cues.zh: 假設你擁有一家公司，販售某種產品，並撰寫文章刊登在網站上。

cues.en: In that article, you claim that your product is able to do certain things.
cues.zh: 文章宣稱你的產品具備某些功能。

cues.en: That is actually not true.
cues.zh: 但那些功能其實並不存在。

cues.en: So obviously that is a fake news, right?
cues.zh: 那顯然就是假新聞。

cues.en: And the reason why you created that article, because you want to get a lot of people purchasing your product.
cues.zh: 你製作這篇文章，是為了吸引更多人購買產品。

cues.en: It's obviously a financial motives, right.
cues.zh: 這顯然是經濟上的動機。

cues.en: So yeah, those are six factors that contribute to the wide spread of fake news and misinformation.
cues.zh: 以上就是促使假新聞與錯誤資訊廣泛流傳的六個因素。

cues.en: Guys, I'll see you guys in the next video where we are going to set up our Google collab.
cues.zh: 下支影片將設定 Google Colab。

cues.en: So I'll see you guys there.
cues.zh: 我們下支影片見。
